meta.title: Who really said "You are never too old to set another goal, or to dream a new dream"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not C.S. Lewis. This popular line has no source in his works — its earliest documented appearance is motivational speaker Les Brown's 1992 book Live Your Dreams.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'You are never too old to set another goal, or to dream a new dream'?
meta.ogDescription: Not C.S. Lewis. Quote Investigator traces this line to motivational speaker Les Brown's 1992 book Live Your Dreams — it appears in none of Lewis's works.

answer.label: Not C.S. Lewis — actually Les Brown
answer.sourceLine: There is no evidence C.S. Lewis ever wrote or said this — it appears in none of his books, letters, or in The Quotable Lewis. Quote Investigator traces the earliest documented appearance to motivational speaker Les Brown’s 1992 book Live Your Dreams, and credits Brown as the likely originator.

source.heading: The real trail
source.excerpt: You are never too old to set another goal or to dream a new dream.
trail: Quote Investigator found no substantive evidence tying the line to C.S. Lewis; its earliest match is Les Brown’s 1992 book Live Your Dreams.
Lewis specialist William O’Flaherty of the Essential C.S. Lewis project concluded the Lewis attribution is incorrect and that Les Brown was the likely creator.
A Check Your Fact review rated the Lewis attribution false, noting it does not appear in The Quotable Lewis or his published works and citing Lewis scholar Michael Ward.
By 1998 the line was reprinted in the Chicken Soup for the Soul series and in Daily Riches — both crediting Les Brown, not Lewis, per Quote Investigator.
source.excerptNote: As documented by Quote Investigator in Les Brown’s 1992 book Live Your Dreams, in a section titled “Never Too Old to Be Bold.” No comparable wording has been found in any work by C.S. Lewis.
source.rightsNote: The earliest documented source is Les Brown’s Live Your Dreams, first published in 1992 by William Morrow & Company — well after 1931, so the wording is in copyright to Brown and his publisher. It is not a public-domain Lewis line, because it is not a Lewis line at all.

author.name: Les Brown
author.heading: Who actually wrote it
author.bio: Les Brown is an American motivational speaker, author, and former Ohio state legislator known for high-energy self-help seminars. The line first appears in documented form in his 1992 book Live Your Dreams, in a passage headed “Never Too Old to Be Bold.” It was later spread through the Chicken Soup for the Soul series before being mistakenly reassigned to C.S. Lewis online.

misattribution.heading: How it got pinned on Lewis
misattribution.intro: This is a classic feel-good misattribution: an uplifting, quotable line drifts onto a beloved literary name that lends it authority. C.S. Lewis is one of the internet’s biggest magnets for such quotes.

items.why: The line appears in none of Lewis’s books, essays, or letters, and is absent from The Quotable Lewis. Quote Investigator found no substantive evidence connecting it to him.
The earliest documented appearance is Brown’s 1992 book Live Your Dreams; by 1998 it circulated in the Chicken Soup series, still credited to Brown, per Quote Investigator.

misattribution.truthLine: No evidence ties this line to C.S. Lewis; the earliest documented source is motivational speaker Les Brown’s 1992 book Live Your Dreams, per Quote Investigator.

context.heading: Why it matters
lead: The sentiment is old — Quote Investigator notes thematic cousins going back to Adelaide Anne Procter’s 1859 verse and the 1881 line “It is never too late to be what you might have been.” But the specific modern wording here belongs to the self-help era, not to Oxford’s mid-century Christian apologist.
Attaching it to C.S. Lewis borrows a literary halo the phrase never earned. The honest credit — a 1990s motivational speaker — is no less inspiring, just accurate.
context.pull: An uplifting line drifts onto a famous name that lends it borrowed authority.
